title: Nested Sports & Teams Checkboxes
description: Build a nested checkbox UI for selecting sports and their teams. Each sport type has child teams. Checking a sport should check all its teams; unchecking any team should uncheck the sport; and when all teams under a sport are checked, the sport should become checked as well. This exercise practices working with hierarchical data, derived state, and checkbox handling.
requirements: Define two local arrays: one for sports types and one for teams.
Each sport type should have: id (number), name (string), and a list of teamIds: number[].
Each team should have: id (number) and name (string).
Render a nested list where each sport type is a parent row with its own checkbox and label.
Under each sport type, render its teams as child rows, each with its own checkbox and label.
Use React.useState to track which sports and teams are currently checked.
When a sport type's checkbox is checked, all of its teams should become checked.
When a sport type's checkbox is unchecked, all of its teams should become unchecked.
When any team under a sport is unchecked, that sport type should become unchecked.
When all teams under a sport are checked, that sport type should become checked.
Do not duplicate data between sports and teams; use the teamIds list on each sport to relate them.
Export the SportsTeamSelector component as the default export.

browserTests.name: Checking a sport checks all its teams
Unchecking a team unchecks the parent sport
Checking all teams checks the parent sport

hints: Keep sports and teams in separate arrays, and use teamIds on each sport to relate them.
Consider using a Set<number> in state to track checked team ids; Sets make adding/removing ids straightforward.
A sport is checked when all of its teamIds are present in the checkedTeams Set.
When a sport checkbox is toggled, add or remove all of its teamIds from the checkedTeams Set.
When a team checkbox is toggled, add or remove just that team id, and derive the sport's checked state from the updated Set instead of storing it separately.
